gap: No result ChatGPT got states which Apple-silicon Macs can feed both inputs of a dual-monitor DisplayPort KVM. Apple's documents show that an M2 MacBook Air drives only one external display. An M3 MacBook Air or MacBook Pro drives two only with the lid closed, and the second display tops out at 4K 100 Hz. An M4 or M5 MacBook Air drives two at up to 4K 144 Hz each. The M3 limit means a dual-4K-144 Hz KVM such as the TESmart DKS202-M24 cannot run both screens at 144 Hz from an M3 Mac.
standout_why: I could not open the cited TESmart DKS202-M24 page (tesmart.com returned HTTP 429 four times), so I can't say what it states. Compared against the other top results: dockgearhq.com (2026-09-12) says only that 'Original M1 MacBook Air machines natively drive one external display' and that M4 MacBook Pro configurations can drive two. It says nothing on M2, nothing on the M3 lid-closed rule, and nothing on the M3 second display's 4K 100 Hz limit. gearexplained.com/guides/dual-monitor-kvm-switch does not mention Apple silicon at all. TESmart's own Common Questions article covers only M1 ('limited to a single monitor'). Separately, ChatGPT told shoppers to prioritize EDID emulation and then made the CKL 622DP-4 its budget pick, but CKL's own listing says that model 'does not support EDID emulation'. Level1Techs' page says the same of its switch ('does not support monitor emulation'). None of the rival pages I read flags either point.
decides: For a MacBook user this decides which switch to buy. With an M1 or M2 MacBook Air, no dual-input switch will work: only one of the two inputs gets a signal, so a DisplayLink-type dock is the route. TESmart's FAQ says this for M1, and Apple's spec page confirms the one-display limit for the M2 Air. With an M3 MacBook Air or MacBook Pro, the switch works only with the lid closed, an external keyboard and mouse, and macOS 14.3 or later (14.6 on the Pro). The second screen is capped at 4K 100 Hz, so a dual 4K 144 Hz switch like the DKS202-M24 or StarTech gives no gain on screen 2. With an M4 or M5 MacBook Air, both screens can run at 4K 144 Hz, which suits the DKS202-M24. For anyone who weighs EDID, as ChatGPT told them to, the $149.99 CKL 622DP-4 drops out: its maker says it has no EDID emulation, and CKL's EDID version, the 622DP-5, is $379. The Level1Techs switch has no EDID emulation either.

findings.label: External displays supported
findings.value: One external display, up to 6K at 60 Hz
findings.note: Apple's Display Support section. One external display means only one of the KVM's two video inputs per computer can be used.

findings.product: general (Apple MacBook Air / MacBook Pro M3)
findings.label: Conditions for two external displays
findings.value: Lid must be closed. Needs an external keyboard and mouse or trackpad, power, and macOS Sonoma 14.3 or later (Air) or 14.6 or later (Pro). Primary display up to 6K 60 Hz or 4K 144 Hz; secondary up to 5K 60 Hz or 4K 100 Hz.
findings.source_title: Use dual monitors with your MacBook Air and MacBook Pro with M3 chip - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple: if you open the lid with both displays connected, 'the secondary external display will go dark or disconnect.' So on an M3 the second screen of a dual 4K 144 Hz KVM is capped at 4K 100 Hz.

findings.label: External displays supported
findings.value: Two external displays plus the built-in screen. With two connected, each runs up to 6K 60 Hz or 4K 144 Hz. With one connected, up to 8K 60 Hz, 5K 120 Hz or 4K 240 Hz.
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Air - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple says to connect displays to the Thunderbolt 4 ports and that closing the lid does not add displays. Each Thunderbolt port needs its own USB-C-to-DP cable into a separate KVM input.

findings.label: Video connections required per computer; Mac limits
findings.value: 2 video connections per computer for dual monitors. M1 Macs are limited to one monitor and need a DisplayLink dock for two. TESmart's DKS201/DKS401 models do not support MST.
findings.note: Part I Q8: 'Each computer needs 2 video connections for the dual monitors to work.' Same FAQ: 'Keyboard software such as Logitech Options, DAS Q, Corsair iCUE, etc. conflicts with the emulation'; the workaround is the USB 2.0/3.0 port, where hotkeys don't work.
